d.chapter: Economic Geography — Natural Regions: 3. Desert Regions
d.notions: Aridity, nomadism, adaptation, foggara, desalination, camel.
d.focus: Problems faced by people in hot deserts and their adaptations.
d.competence: Learners are able to save water and protect themselves from heat and dust, as desert people do.
objectives: Identify the problems faced by people living in hot deserts.
Describe the traditional adaptations of desert people.
Describe the modern adaptations used in deserts.
recall: Desert vegetation is scarce: cacti, thorny bushes and date palms in oases.
Plants store water, reduce water loss and have long roots.
Desert soils are sandy or stony, salty and poor in humus.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: problems of a week in the Sahara.
situation: A Tuareg family lives in the Sahara, in northern Niger. The only well near their camp has dried up, and there is no grass left for their camels and goats.
The father must decide what to do to save his family and his animals.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that the Tuareg family has no more water and no grass for their animals.
Which animals does the family rear?
The family rears camels and goats.
What can the father do to save his family and animals?
He can move with his family and animals to another place where there is a well and pasture.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the difficulties of life in the desert and the clever ways people adapt to them.

qa.q: What is the biggest problem for people and animals living in hot deserts?
qa.a: The biggest problem is the lack of water for drinking, washing, animals and farming.

qa.q: Give two problems caused by the desert climate for people's health.
qa.a: The strong heat can cause heatstroke and dehydration, and the dust of sandstorms causes eye and breathing problems.

qa.q: Why is it difficult to build roads and travel in the desert?
qa.a: The distances are very long, moving dunes cover roads, and there are few towns and water points.

sum.title: I. Problems Faced
sum.intro: The main problems faced by people in hot deserts are the following:
items: A. Lack of Water
Water is very scarce for drinking, washing, animals and farming.
B. Extreme Temperatures
Very hot days cause heatstroke and dehydration. Nights can be very cold.
C. Sandstorms and Moving Dunes
Sandstorms cause eye and breathing problems. Moving dunes bury roads, wells and fields.
D. Poor Soils and Isolation
Soils are poor and salty, so farming is difficult. Towns are far apart and transport is difficult.

qa.q: Why is the camel called the "ship of the desert"?
qa.a: The camel can walk for days without drinking, carry heavy loads, and walk easily on sand with its wide feet.

qa.q: Why do the Tuareg and the Bedouin move from place to place with their animals?
qa.a: They move in search of water and pasture. This way of life is called nomadism.

qa.q: How do desert people protect themselves from the sun and the sand?
qa.a: They wear long, loose, light-coloured clothes and cover their heads and faces with a turban or a veil.

qa.q: Rich desert countries such as Saudi Arabia have little fresh water. How do they get drinking water for their cities?
qa.a: They remove the salt from sea water in factories. This is called desalination.

sum.title: II. Adaptations
sum.intro: People have adapted to life in hot deserts in the following ways:
items: A. Nomadism
Nomads, such as the Tuareg and the Bedouin, move with their animals in search of water and pasture.
B. Use of the Camel
The camel can live for days without water and carry heavy loads across the sand.
C. Clothing and Housing
People wear long, loose, light clothes and turbans. Houses have thick mud walls, small windows and flat roofs.
D. Water Supply
People dig wells and underground channels called foggaras. Rich countries use desalination of sea water.
E. Modern Technology
Air conditioning, solar energy and paved roads make life easier in desert towns.

evaluation: What is the main problem of life in the desert?
The main problem of life in the desert is the lack of water.
What is nomadism? Name one nomadic people of the Sahara.
Nomadism is moving from place to place with animals in search of water and pasture. The Tuareg are nomads of the Sahara.
Desalination is the removal of salt from sea water to obtain fresh water.
remediation: The animal called the "ship of the desert" is the ______.
Moving from place to place with animals is called ______.
A nomadic people of the Sahara is the ______.
Underground water channels in the Sahara are called ______.
Removing salt from sea water is called ______.
Desert houses have thick ______ walls to keep them cool.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. camel 2. nomadism 3. Tuareg 4. foggaras 5. desalination 6. mud
d.homework: Find in your textbook or atlas the name of one oasis in the Sahara, and write the name of the country where it is found.
